newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Wing Tiek to settle $90 mln in Manila deal.
newsitem.headline: Wing Tiek to settle $90 mln in Manila deal.

text.p: Malaysia's Wing Tiek Holdings Berhad said on Friday it would pay by the end of this month the remaining $90 million of the $150 million due to the government as payment for a majority stake in National Steel Corp (NSC).

This would be paid in three tranches: an initial $20 million; another $50 million from its partner Marubeni Corp as soon as the property issue is settled; and the final $20 million by Sept 30, 1996, Wing Tiek said in a statement.
Marubeni has pledged to pay the $50 million due on Sept 15 upon the completion of NSC's land divestment program, Wing Tiek said.
The property issue referred to is an agreement by the state-owned NSC to sell its land holdings to a new venture.
A Philippine law allows foreign firms to own only up to 40 percent of a property in the country.
Wing Tiek has bought a 75 percent stake in NSC which owns about 600 hectares of land.
Wing Tiek and the government had agreed the land should be sold to a new venture in which the NSC would have a 40 percent stake.
Besides the $150 million payment to the government, Wing Tiek has also agreed to infuse new equity worth 2.3 billion pesos ($88 million). This is due by October 31.
NSC accounts for over 40 percent of the local steel output with an annual production capacity of 3.5 million tonnes.
